# 2 Kings Chapter 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 226r–227r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_005_page_001.jpg, 2KI_005_page_002.jpg, 2KI_005_page_003.jpg

---

**5:1** And-Na'aman, commander of-the-army [sar tseva] of-the-king of-Aram, was a-great man before his-master and-lifted of-face [nesu fanim], for through-him YHWH had-given victory [teshu'ah] to-Aram. And-the-man was a-mighty warrior [gibbor chayil], [but] a-leper [metsora'].

**5:2** And-Aram had-gone-out [in] bands [gedudim] and-had-captured from-the-land of-Yisra'el a-small girl [na'arah qetannah], and-she-was before the-wife of-Na'aman.

**5:3** And-she-said to-her-mistress: If-only [achaley] my-master [were] before the-prophet who [is] in-Shomron! Then he-would-gather-him [ye'esof] from-his-leprosy [tsara'ato].

**5:4** And-he-went and-told his-master, saying: Thus and-thus spoke the-girl who [is] from-the-land of-Yisra'el.

**5:5** And-said the-king of-Aram: Go, come [lekh bo], and-I-will-send a-letter to the-king of-Yisra'el. And-he-went and-took in-his-hand ten talents [kikkar] of-silver and-six-thousand [pieces] of-gold and-ten changes [chalifot] of-garments.

**5:6** And-he-brought the-letter to the-king of-Yisra'el, saying: And-now, when-this letter comes to-you, behold, I-have-sent to-you Na'aman my-servant, and-you-shall-gather-him from-his-leprosy.

**5:7** And-it-was when-the-king of-Yisra'el read the-letter, and-he-tore his-garments and-said: Am-I God [ha-elohim anokhi], to-kill and-to-make-alive, that this-one sends to-me to-gather a-man from-his-leprosy? For know, please, and-see that he [is] seeking-occasion [mitanneh] against-me.

**5:8** And-it-was when-Elisha the-man of-God heard that the-king of-Yisra'el had-torn his-garments, and-he-sent to the-king, saying: Why have-you-torn your-garments? Let-him-come, please, to-me, and-he-shall-know that there-is a-prophet in-Yisra'el.

**5:9** And-came Na'aman with-his-horses and-with-his-chariot and-stood at-the-opening of-the-house of-Elisha.

**5:10** And-sent to-him Elisha a-messenger, saying: Go and-wash [rachats] in-the-Yarden seven times [sheva pe'amim], and-your-flesh shall-return [yashuv] to-you and-be-clean [u-tehar].

**5:11** And-was-angry [vayiqtsof] Na'aman and-went and-said: Behold, I-said [to myself], he-will-surely come-out to-me and-stand and-call in-the-name of-YHWH his-God and-wave [heynif] his-hand over the-place and-gather the-leper.

**5:12** Are-not Amanah and-Pharpar, rivers of-Dammeseq, better [tovim] than-all the-waters of-Yisra'el? Could-I-not wash in-them and-be-clean? And-he-turned and-went in-rage [be-chemah].

**5:13** And-drew-near his-servants and-spoke to-him and-said: My-father [avi], [if] the-prophet had-spoken to-you a-great thing [davar gadol], would-you-not do-it? How-much-more [aph ki] when-he-said to-you: Wash and-be-clean?

**5:14** And-he-went-down and-dipped [vayitbol] in-the-Yarden seven times, according-to-the-word of-the-man of-God, and-his-flesh returned [vatashov] like-the-flesh of-a-small boy [na'ar qaton], and-he-was-clean.

**5:15** And-he-returned to the-man of-God, he and-all his-camp, and-he-came and-stood before-him and-said: Behold, please, I-know that there-is-no God in-all the-earth except in-Yisra'el. And-now, take, please, a-blessing [berakhah] from your-servant.

**5:16** And-he-said: As-YHWH-lives, before-whom I-stand, I-will-not take [lo eqqach]. And-he-pressed-him to-take, and-he-refused.

**5:17** And-said Na'aman: And-if not, let-there-be-given, please, to-your-servant a-load of-a-pair of-mules [massa tsemed peradim] of-earth [adamah], for your-servant will-no-more make a-burnt-offering ['olah] or-sacrifice [zevach] to-other gods, but to-YHWH.

**5:18** In-this thing may-YHWH pardon [yislach] your-servant: when-my-master goes into-the-house of-Rimmon to-bow-down there, and-he [is] leaning on-my-arm, and-I-bow-down in-the-house of-Rimmon — when-I-bow-down in-the-house of-Rimmon, may-YHWH, please, pardon your-servant in-this thing.

**5:19** And-he-said to-him: Go in-peace [lekh le-shalom]. And-he-went from-him a-stretch of-land [kivrat arets].

**5:20** And-said Gechazi, servant of-Elisha the-man of-God: Behold, my-master has-spared [chasakh] this Na'aman the-Aramean, not-taking from-his-hand what he-brought. As-YHWH-lives, I-will-run after-him and-take from-him something [me'umah].

**5:21** And-pursued Gechazi after Na'aman. And-saw Na'aman [one] running after-him, and-he-fell from the-chariot to-meet-him and-said: Is-[all]-well [ha-shalom]?

**5:22** And-he-said: [All is] well [shalom]. My-master has-sent-me, saying: Behold, just-now two youths [ne'arim] have-come to-me from-the-hill-country of-Efrayim, from-the-sons of-the-prophets. Give, please, to-them a-talent of-silver and-two changes of-garments.

**5:23** And-said Na'aman: Be-willing [ho'el], take two-talents. And-he-urged-him and-bound two-talents of-silver in-two bags and-two changes of-garments, and-gave [them] to-two of-his-servants, and-they-carried [them] before-him.

**5:24** And-he-came to the-hill [ha-ofel] and-took [them] from-their-hand and-deposited [them] in-the-house, and-he-sent the-men away, and-they-went.

**5:25** And-he-came and-stood before his-master. And-said to-him Elisha: From-where [me-ayin], Gechazi? And-he-said: Your-servant did-not go anywhere [lo halakh aneh va-anah].

**5:26** And-he-said to-him: Did-not my-heart [libbi] go, when the-man turned from-upon his-chariot to-meet-you? Is-[this] a-time to-take silver and-to-take garments, and-olive-groves and-vineyards, and-sheep and-cattle, and-male-servants and-female-servants?

**5:27** And-the-leprosy of-Na'aman shall-cling [tidbaq] to-you and-to-your-seed forever ['ad olam]. And-he-went-out from-before-him, leprous [metsora'] like-the-snow.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — YHWH had given victory to Aram:** A remarkable theological statement — Israel's God gives military success to Israel's enemy through a pagan general. YHWH's sovereignty is not limited to Israel.

**v.12 — Amanah and Pharpar:** The Amanah (modern Barada) and Pharpar (possibly the Awaj) are the rivers of Damascus. Naaman's pride is geographical: Syrian rivers are superior. His anger is about dignity — he expected a dramatic healing ceremony, not a simple command.

**v.17 — earth from Israel:** Naaman's request for two mule-loads of Israelite soil reflects ancient belief that deities were connected to specific territories. He will worship YHWH on YHWH's own soil, even in Damascus.

**v.18 — house of Rimmon:** Rimmon = Hadad, the Aramean storm god. Naaman asks in advance for forgiveness for the unavoidable civic duty of accompanying his king into the pagan temple. Elisha's "Go in peace" is neither condemnation nor explicit permission — a deliberately open response.

**v.27 — leprous like the snow:** The transfer of leprosy from Naaman to Gehazi completes the moral reversal: the foreign general gains health and faith; the Israelite servant gains disease and judgment.

*— EMET*
